A1.justification: Both PDFs describe Fast3Dcache and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. Retained material can be matched reliably despite supplementary-section and figure renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original TRELLIS/DSO experiments, acceleration and geometry measurements, component ablations, and qualitative generation results in the main text and appendix.

after.justification: V2 retains these original experiments and adds text-to-3D, OmniObject3D, data-driven calibration, and additional sensitivity results.

M1.justification: Section 7.4 adds an alternative PCSC calibration procedure: fit per-instance slopes with RANSAC and use their median as a dataset-specific slope. This supplements v1's fixed parameter selection; the core PCSC/SSC equations, three-phase inference, and Algorithm 1 remain unchanged.

E1.justification: V1's quantitative coverage centers on Toys4K image-to-3D generation using TRELLIS/DSO. V2 retains this and adds OmniObject3D image-to-3D evaluation and text-conditioned generation on TRELLIS-text-xlarge, substantially extending data and task coverage (Section 7.3, Tables 6–7).

E2.justification: The retained comparisons use the same vanilla models, RAS, TeaCache, and EasyCache, including the existing combinations with Fast3Dcache. The new dataset/task comparisons reuse vanilla TRELLIS and RAS. Section 7.1 clarifies RAS implementation without establishing a changed comparator.

E3.justification: New experiments introduce TRELLIS-text-xlarge with CLIP scoring, OmniObject3D evaluation using 216 objects and four views each, and calibration using 100 sampled instances per dataset and steps 8–18. Additional parameter settings are evaluated in Table 11. The original Toys4K protocol remains unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds a default-versus-fitted slope analysis (Figure 5, Table 8) and finer slope and refresh-interval sweeps (Table 11). These extend existing parameter investigations; the original component ablations, sampling-schedule analyses, and qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Section 7.4 and Figure 5 introduce statistical slope estimation using random instance sampling, RANSAC, outlier filtering, and median aggregation, with distributions shown for both datasets. These are sample-based parameter estimates; repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, and significance tests remain unreported.

E6.justification: Tables 6–8 and 11 add substantial benchmark and parameter-analysis results. For example, the new text-to-3D comparison reports 0.4781 iter/s and CLIP 19.3325 at τ = 8, versus vanilla's 0.3507 and 22.9684. Retained benchmark values, including the renumbered phase-three ablations, are unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, Equations 1–8, sampling-schedule reasoning, and FLOPs derivations are retained. Renaming total inference steps from N to T and clarifying index-set notation do not change the mathematics. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The training-free geometry-aware caching claim, PCSC/SSC contributions, and headline efficiency–fidelity claims remain the same. V2's explicit sparse-voxel emphasis restates scope already documented in v1. The abstract's 54.8% to 54.83% FLOPs reduction is equivalent rounding of the existing result.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations concerning data-driven calibration and local parameter robustness. Section 13 adds discussion of SLAT acceleration and future texture-specific constraints. Section 7.3 also characterizes the new task results as having negligible quality loss, although Table 6 shows a CLIP decline.

D1.justification: Section 7.1 newly specifies RAS starvation prevention and application to DSO without modifications; Sections 7.3–7.4 document additional rendering and calibration details. The release promise becomes a statement that code and models are publicly available. Existing hardware, default hyperparameters, and the project-page link are retained.

R1.justification: V2 adds the OmniObject3D citation supporting its new evaluation. The related-work discussion and substantive positioning against existing acceleration methods remain essentially unchanged. Other reference renumbering and publication-metadata updates concern already cited works.

P1.justification: Localized edits improve section introductions, terminology, captions, and the Section 10 title, while expanding author affiliations. The appendix becomes Supplementary Material, and Section 7 gains subsections for the additions. The main narrative and section organization are largely retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds four compact supplementary tables and the four-panel calibration Figure 5. Most existing visuals are retained and renumbered. Figure 4 is reduced in size, Algorithm 1 expands from one column to page width, and supplementary figures and tables are repositioned.

improvement.justification: The additional dataset/task evaluations and calibration/sensitivity studies make generalization and parameter choices better supported, while implementation and availability disclosures aid reproducibility. The gain is limited by sparse text-to-3D protocol documentation and overstated interpretation: Section 7.3 calls quality loss negligible despite CLIP falling from 22.9684 to 19.3325 at τ = 8 in Table 6.
